newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo rises on robust earnings increase.
newsitem.headline: Anglo rises on robust earnings increase.

text.p: Shares in Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd jumped at the start of trade on Wednesday on the back of a solid 23 percent rise in year earnings released after the market's close on Tuesday.
At 0737 GMT Anglo was up 125 cents or almost 0.5 percent to 269.50 rand after a small volume of 4,100 shares had changed hands.
"Those results were pretty much in the middle of what people were expecting. There's nothing to be disappointed about," a Johannesburg Stock Exchange dealer said.
"The share was also offering some good value at the 260 rand level," he added.

The rise in earnings at South Africa's biggest firm to a headline per share figure of 2,144 cents was broadly in line with analysts' expectations but the dividend proved a pleasant surprise coming in at 700 cents compared to an expected 690.
Anglo said associates had contributed strongly to the earnings improvement.

"The associates' contribution of 7,597 million rand to net income before taxation rose by 25 percent, largely as a result of much improved operating results from diamonds, gold and mining finance interests," Anglo said in a statement.
Analysts said rich profits from sister companies diamond giant De Beers Consolidated and offshore mining financial company Minorco SA had contributed to Anglo's earnings.
